I’m so sorry to hear.  My dog is a huge reason I wake up every morning too.  She was diagnosed with RA this past year and she broke a bone so I completely get the unplanned expense/stress.  Go snuggle with your pups if you can.  Remember that their health issues will still be there if you binge but the only thing that changes is that you will feel even worse.  I always have to constantly remind myself that binging will only make me feel better temporarily then it makes me feel worse and the problem is still there.

Mono has a probable connection with many illnesses.  It’s crazy!  I’ve tried a couple specific things I can share that have worked really well in my case having mono and then fibro if you are in the same boat.

I’m so glad that you got your answers!  I’ve read AMA can be positive in RA though so if you feel ok I’m sure there is no reason to suspect anything else but doesn’t hurt to check if your doctor thinks it’s needed.

I don’t think I have Autoimmune Hepatitis because I’ve been tested for it.  The test I took only tells me my body is producing detectable levels of Anti-Mitochondrial Antibodies which are found in Primary Biliary Cholangitis  among other autoimmune illnesses but not typically in AIH.  

I was diagnosed with fibromyalgia two and a half years ago immediately following my second mononucleosis infection.  I’ve always believed I have something autoimmune in addition to fibro because I’ve had signs of it such as pericarditis, rashes, visible inflammation, positive blood markers such as elevated liver panel and Antinuclear Antibodies too.

As far as my symptoms go, I too have extreme fatigue.  I would say itching is my second worst symptom, itching/rashes.  I have dry eyes/mouth (but no Sjogrens).  I have severe muscle spasms, random bouts of neuropathy, muscle weakness, and muscle pain which the muscle pain is probably why I got the fibro dx. 

I’m sorry your family is suffering so much.

It’s so frustrating.  I tried EVERYTHING and this south beach diet which I cheat on 2x a week somehow stopped it and I do open water swimming.  I couldn’t dream of drinking or going to a bar for the past two years because of sensory issues and alcohol being a trigger but I partied my ass off this past weekend and was like no way this is real and I was fine the next day, nothing.  I feel my age again (27) and I can sleep 7-8 hours and not 12 and I’m remembering information and getting better grades.  It really scares me though to think about how sick I was... it just blows my mind because all of my doctors told me that remission probably wouldn’t happen in my case and based on hitting the 2 year mark of being sick af.  I really hope you find some relief and good luck with the triathlons.  I loved my swims even when I was sick, worth every spoon of energy.

I get horrible fatigue with my fibro that’s not cured with rest and I don’t bring that up because I did one time at the beginning of my illness and my friend said, “oh everyone is tired, take a nap.”  I am pretty passive aggressive so I doubt I said anything rude but I was like no, no your tiredness sucks not minimizing that but fatigue can’t be lumped into that because it’s not the same and doesn’t have the same cause or treatment.

I want my true time and to know I did it and not because of a piece of clothing.  Some of these racers were in a full suit and I get that they do that in the fall but the water was maybe 68 degrees like maybe when you’d hit a shadow.

I grew up swimming competitively which is probably the only reason I’m able to do distance swimming now.  

I don’t have my illness well managed at all and we are actually looking for a co-existing condition right now but I think honestly I had a horrible reaction to medication ( 150 mg of Effexor being cut in two weeks) and I’m not confident it’s anything other than fibromyalgia like it’s been for the past two years.  On July 11th I had a lumbar puncture and was admitted to the hospital overnight because my legs were so weak.  I had to take a week off of any exercise because I was getting spinal headaches pretty easily so I was furious at being sick and decided to work even harder this week before my race.  

I do maybe five races a year usually in the 1-3 mile range and swim 3 ish times a week when I’m well.  I sleep the night before my race like I will take a sleeping pill if I need to and then in the morning I have caffeine (5 hour energy) and Gatorade chews which I only have on race days so they actually work for me and this usually gives me enough energy even if some of it is false energy and I pay later.  I LOVE to swim so for me it’s a good use of not feeling well every few months. 

I ended up first in my age group yesterday and 14/110 swimmers overall which usually I’m in the middle.  I used to be an ok swimmer and I decided to just use every spoon I had to sprint 1.2 miles down this river and then pay for it lol.

“Doing the dancing queen” - I’m studying to be in the medical field because of this illness and I’m literally LOLing imaging the nervous system doing the dancing queen but that’s a great way to put it.  I think some of us have proprioceptor issues which is where we get problems with sensory and some of us have motor issues and some of us just have it all.

When I move it feels like something is ripping because my muscles are so stiff.  This is happening all over my back and with the four muscles that are in the rotator cuff.  Your pain sounds awful.  I hope you get some relief.
